title: The two-qubit singlet/triplet measurement is universal for quantum computing given only maximally-mixed initial states
relevance: Established universality of ideal adaptive STP from maximally mixed input.

title: Symmetry Protected Quantum Computation
authors: Michael H. Freedman; Matthew B. Hastings; Modjtaba Shokrian Zini
relevance: STP model, protection motivation, and relationships with permutational and postselected computation. Its universality conjecture was subsequently resolved.

title: Permutational Quantum Computing
relevance: A computational model built from spin coupling and permutations; historical background rather than an assertion that its original open problems remain open.

title: Optimal Qubit Purification and Unitary Schur Sampling via Random SWAP Tests
authors: Shrigyan Brahmachari; Austin Hulse; Henry D. Pfister; Iman Marvian
relevance: Random pairwise SWAP-test protocols for specified qubit purification and Schur-sampling tasks. Does not establish an arbitrary coherent Schur transform.

title: A complexity phase transition at the EPR Hamiltonian
relevance: Proved Hamiltonian classification, EPR* tractability question, and named singlet conjecture.

title: Complexity classification of local Hamiltonian problems
relevance: Background classification of two-local Hamiltonians. Match signs, weights, and graph restrictions to the precise result used.

title: Testing product states, quantum Merlin-Arthur games and tensor optimisation
relevance: Product-state testing and applications to unentangled witnesses.

title: A quantum oracle separation between QMA(2) and QMA
authors: John Bostanci; Sabee Grewal; Jonas Haferkamp; Andrew Huang; Yeongwoo Hwang; Anand Natarajan; Chinmay Nirkhe
relevance: A quantum-oracle separation using symmetric/antisymmetric projectors; also gives disentangler lower bounds. It is not an unrelativized separation.

title: Symmetry-assisted adversaries for quantum state generation
authors: Andris Ambainis; Loïck Magnin; Martin Roetteler; Jérémie Roland
relevance: Representation theory in adversary bounds and quantum state generation.

title: Quantum Lazy Sampling and Path Recording for Any Group
authors: Ben Foxman; Alex Lombardi; Fermi Ma; Barak Nehoran; John Wright
relevance: Purification, representation theory, and recording access to random group elements.

title: The Compressed Oracle is a Worthy (Multiplicative) Adversary
relevance: Connects compressed-oracle methods with multiplicative adversaries; useful background for the requested purification/adversary bridge.

title: A General Quantum Duality for Representations of Groups with Applications to Quantum Money, Lightning, and Fire
authors: John Bostanci; Barak Nehoran; Mark Zhandry
relevance: Computational relationship between implementing representations and Fourier subspace extraction, with applications to quantum cryptography.

title: Optimal Quantum de Finetti Theorems via Argmax Rounding
authors: Fernando Granha Jeronimo; Pei Wu; Haochen Xu
relevance: Quantum de Finetti and disentangling constructions. Input dimension, number of qubits, and approximation conventions matter when comparing bounds.

title: Efficient Quantum Circuits for Schur and Clebsch–Gordan Transforms
authors: Dave Bacon; Isaac L. Chuang; Aram W. Harrow
relevance: Efficient coherent Schur and Clebsch–Gordan transforms; the representation-theoretic coordinate system.

title: Tight Bounds for Inverting Permutations via Compressed Oracle Arguments
relevance: Purified random-permutation oracles, representation theory, and lower bounds.

title: Spectral gap of Lee-Yang Hamiltonians
relevance: A uniform-field spectral-gap theorem yielding BQP ground-energy estimation for Lee–Yang Hamiltonians; applies to EPR*.

title: Lee-Yang tensors and Hamiltonian complexity
authors: Benjamin Wong; Sergey Bravyi; David Gosset; Yinchen Liu
relevance: The Lee–Yang tensor and Hamiltonian framework, including the EPR adiabatic approach and earlier gap conjectures.

title: Guidable Local Hamiltonian Problems with Implications to Heuristic Ansätze State Preparation and the Quantum PCP Conjecture
authors: Jordi Weggemans; Marten Folkertsma; Chris Cade
relevance: QCMA formulations in which a suitable guiding state is promised to exist. A direct framework for the classical-starting-data question; it does not establish guides for every stoquastic YES instance.

title: Monte Carlo simulation of stoquastic Hamiltonians
relevance: Projection Monte Carlo and MA verification with specified classical guiding-state promises. Those promises are additional assumptions, not consequences of stoquasticity alone.

title: Quantum fingerprinting
authors: Harry Buhrman; Richard Cleve; John Watrous; Ronald de Wolf
relevance: Quantum-state comparison with the SWAP test and its application to communication complexity. The overlap formula assumes independent inputs.

title: Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
relevance: Chapters 11 and 15 develop representation theory, Fourier transforms, and Schur–Weyl duality. Background for the exposition of irreps, multiplicities, and coupling paths.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Representation-Theoretic Multiplicities
relevance: Generalized-phase-estimation algorithms for multiplicities with specified dimension-ratio restrictions. Some proposed superpolynomial speedups were refuted by subsequent classical algorithms; consult Panova alongside this paper.

title: Polynomial time classical versus quantum algorithms for representation theoretic multiplicities
relevance: Classical polynomial-time algorithms for many representation-theoretic multiplicity families previously proposed for quantum speedups, refuting some earlier conjectures.

title: Discovering a new quantum algorithm
relevance: Expository account of representation-theoretic multiplicity algorithms and the classical progress they prompted; mathematical claims here are linked to the primary papers.

title: Forrelation: A Problem That Optimally Separates Quantum from Classical Computing
relevance: A Fourier-correlation problem with a nearly maximal quantum–classical query separation; a benchmark for spin-based oracle questions.

title: The quantum Schur and Clebsch–Gordan transforms: I. Efficient qudit circuits
authors: Dave Bacon; Isaac L. Chuang; Aram W. Harrow
relevance: Efficient Schur transforms for qudits, with explicit dependence on the number of systems, local dimension, and precision.

title: Classical and quantum communication without a shared reference frame
authors: Stephen D. Bartlett; Terry Rudolph; Robert W. Spekkens
relevance: Relational encodings permit classical and quantum communication without a shared spatial reference frame.

title: Reference frames, superselection rules, and quantum information
authors: Stephen D. Bartlett; Terry Rudolph; Robert W. Spekkens
relevance: Reference-frame restrictions, relational information, and resources associated with symmetry in quantum information.

title: The complexity of stoquastic local Hamiltonian problems
authors: Sergey Bravyi; David P. DiVincenzo; Roberto I. Oliveira; Barbara M. Terhal
relevance: Complexity bounds for local Hamiltonians with real nonpositive off-diagonal matrix elements in a specified basis.

title: Complexity of stoquastic frustration-free Hamiltonians
relevance: Classical simulation of specified stoquastic frustration-free adiabatic paths and MA-completeness of stoquastic satisfiability.

title: Exponential algorithmic speedup by quantum walk
authors: Andrew M. Childs; Richard Cleve; Enrico Deotto; Edward Farhi; Sam Gutmann; Daniel A. Spielman
relevance: An exponential oracle separation obtained by coherent graph traversal; a benchmark for walks on coupling and representation graphs.

title: The Church of the Symmetric Subspace
relevance: A survey of symmetric-subspace methods in state estimation, cloning, de Finetti theorems, and concentration bounds.

title: The complexity of antiferromagnetic interactions and 2D lattices
relevance: QMA-completeness of antiferromagnetic Heisenberg interactions with positive weights, together with classifications under interaction and graph restrictions.

title: Universal qudit Hamiltonians
relevance: Universal Hamiltonian families for qudits, including SU(d) and spin-SU(2) Heisenberg interactions.

title: A one-way quantum computer
relevance: Measurement-based computation on cluster states; background for treating adaptive measurement as the computational operation.

title: A relational quantum computer using only two-qubit total spin measurement and an initial supply of highly mixed single qubit states
relevance: An earlier universality construction using singlet–triplet measurements and three suitably chosen single-qubit input states; distinct from maximally mixed input alone.

title: Polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization and discrete logarithms on a quantum computer
relevance: Order finding and Fourier-based quantum algorithms for factoring and discrete logarithms; a target for a direct spin-based formulation.
